eligibility.quote: The problem was that serial.block() is called before serial.open() in hydro branch kobuki_driver/kobuki.cpp line 93

failed_conditions.quote: The description of open() in ecl_core/ecl_device/serial_pos.hpp:line 153 tells that block() needs to be called after serial is opened.

loudness.quote: Also, ecl serial.block() should warn user if file_descriptor is not initialized.

resolution.quote: Thus, the proposed patch is going to call serial.block() function after serial.open() in kobuki.cpp

notes: Sources opened: issue #272 body and comments (gh api) - corot's report ('ROS log gets somehow horribly mangled', 'And prevents Ctrl+C to work.'), bit-pirate's mangled all-caps log (comment 21840623), and jihoonl's full diagnosis (comment 21917240, quoted); kobuki.cpp at ba100858 via raw.githubusercontent (line 93 'serial.block(4000); // blocks by default, but just to be clear!' before serial.open at line 95) and at 0.3.9 (serial.open at line 105, serial.block(4000) at line 110); fix commit 054c753 via gh api (merge of PR #278 'To resolve issue 272. babo terminal', 2013-08-01; diff moves serial.block(4000) to after serial.open/is_connected in Kobuki::init and adds it after the reconnect open in Kobuki::spin); ecl_core 0.60.5 serial_pos.hpp line 144 ('Serial() : is_open(false), error_handler(NoError)' - file_descriptor unset) and serial_pos.cpp line 320 ('tcsetattr(file_descriptor, TCSAFLUSH, &options);') via raw.githubusercontent. Eligibility: agree, stop 6. E2 step 1: ecl_devices (provider library, package of stonier/ecl_core) and kobuki_driver (consumer library) are separately released packages. Step 2: the failed interaction is the consumer violating the provider's documented call-order precondition ('By default, the port is configured to read in blocking mode (with overly large timeout of 5s) - use the block(timeout_ms) and unblock() methods to alter its behaviour.' in the open() documentation quoted in the comment) - a wrong ordering crossing the library boundary ('component order'/'timing' in the rubric's step-2 list); with the consumer's own 0.3.9 order the same provider works, and with a provider that guarded block() on an unopened device the same consumer would not mangle the terminal, so the failure depends on the interaction, not on one unit alone. Steps 3-5: resolving change is a source reorder in kobuki_driver, not name/build/firmware. Stop 6, library API. An 'internal' reading (a bug in kobuki_driver's own init sequence) is arguable, but the documented provider precondition crossing the boundary makes interface the better call under this rubric, and the specification's E2 evidence is faithful to the sources. Failed condition: class 'other' agreed (call-order precondition has no dedicated class); elements (block, open) agreed. Loudness silent_documented/activate agreed: no tooling diagnostic (the maintainer himself notes the provider 'should warn user if file_descriptor is not initialized', i.e. it does not); the misuse executes in Kobuki::init at node start-up (activate), visible only as the mangled terminal. Resolution recommended agreed: fix merged the same day as the diagnosis; the issue was closed without a comment showing the terminal problem gone, and the maintainer's working observation ('In the version 0.3.9, which I confirmed that working fine') uses the older consumer rather than the merged fix - S1 puts such evidence in 'recommended'.
